If you would like to participate in this meeting, you can participate via the following options:

1. VIEW THE MEETING ONLINE AT : https://youtube.com/@SouthGateCA90280
Please allow up to 24 hours after the meeting for the archive to be available.
2. PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING by emailing the City Clerk at:
yglaze@sogate.org no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please write "Public
Comment" in the subject line.
3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON

*The disruption in service of any alternative method does not prelude the City Council or other
legislative body from taking further action and moving forward on the agenda.

Meeting Schedule

  1
 The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Call to Order/Roll Call

ROLL CALL:  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

Meeting Compensation Disclosure
Pursuant to Government Code Section 54952.3: Disclosure of compensation for meeting
attendance by City Council Members is $790 monthly regardless of the amount of meetings.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their

  4
 comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  Declaring

  LGBTQ+  Pride  Month
  June  2024

WHEREAS,  all residents  of tis  community  deserve  to be treated  with  dignity,
respect,  compassion  and justice  regardless  of gender,  age, race, religion,  economic
status, or sexual  orientation;  and

WHEREAS,  LGBTQ+  Pride  Month  is a time to recall  the trials  the LGBTQ+
community  has endured  and to rejoice  in the triumphs  of trailblazing  individuals  who
have bravely  fought  and continue  to fight  for full  equality;  and

WHEREAS,  Pride  is a celebration  of visibility,  self-worth,  and dignity  and during
this time,  we recognize  the valuable  contributions  of the LGBTQ+  individuals  across
America,  and we reaffirm  our commitment  to the ongoing  muggle  against
discrimination  and injustice  and are committed  to protecting  the civil  rights  of the
LGBTQ+  community  to create a more  open and just  society;  and

WHEREAS,  the LGBTQ+  cornmunity  in America  has achieved  remarkable  progress
with  historic  Supreme  Court  rulings  in recent years which  have eliminated  regressive
laws, affirmed  the right  to marriage  equality,  and secured  workplace  protection  for
LGBTQ+;  an

WHERJEAS,  the LGBTQ+  community  now serves in nearly  eveiy  level  of public
office  including  local  govemrnent,  the office  of Governor,  to Congress,  and throughout
Administration;  and

WHEREAS,  during  Pride Month,  we recognize  the determination  of many
individuals  who are fighting  to live freely  and authentically  and in doing  so, are opening
hearts and minds,  and laying  the foundation  for a just  and equitable  America.

NOW,  THEREFORE,  be it proclaimed  on this  28'h  day  of May  2024  that  I,  Gil
Hurtado,  Mayor  of the City  of South  Gate,  on behalf  of the City  Council,  do hereby
declare  June 2024,  as LGBTQ+  Pride  Month  and call upon the citizens  of Soutl'i Gate to
stand against  discrimination  and injustice  and to celebrate  and welcome  diversity  and
equality.

  Gil  Hurtado,  Mayor

  Declaring

  National  Post-Traumatic  Stress  Disorder
  Awareness  Month
  June  2024

WHEREAS,  in May,  we are reminded  not only  of the human  mind's  immense  strength
but also some of its limitations.  It is a reminder  that we are not machines,  and that it is
completely  normal  to feel the emotions  that we do. And unlike  macMnes,  we have the
strength  to get better  on our own by helping  each other;  and

WHEREAS,  there are two types of trauma  and they range in the severity  of the causes
and triggers:  the 'Big  T' is any type of trauma  that has occwed  due to a life-threatening
situation  like wars,  nahiral  disasters,  physical  assault,  etc., while  the 'Small  t' is caused
due to a dishirbing  event that is not life-threatening  like divorce,  abnipt  relocation,
financial  woes,  etc.; and

WHEREAS,  many  people  recover  from  PTSD  after a few days, weeks,  or months.
Yet, for others,  the recovery  road might  mean one year or more.  This mental  disorder  is
ighly  treatable,  but due to the lack of knowledge  around  it as well  as the stigma
attached  to seeking  mental  help, many  choose  to ignore  the problem  and suffer  through
it; and

WHEREAS,  June is National  PTSD  Awareness  Month.  Its goal is to raise awareness
about  said mental  illness  for people  to recover  from  it by seeking  better  and effective
treatments  like group  therapy,  counseling,  and antidepressants;  and

WHEREAS,  the more talk there is about  PTSD,  the more people  will  become  aware
of it, and the more people  will  seek treatment  for it. The road to recovery  may look
different  from  one person  to another,  but it is always  there.

NOW,  THEREFORE,  be it proclaimed  on this  28'h  day  of May  2024  that  I,  Gil
Hurtado,  Mayor  of the City  of South  Gate,  on behalf  of the City  Council,  do hereby
proclaim  June 2024,  as National  Post-Traumatic  Stress Disorder  Awareness  Month  and
encourage  citizens  to  learn  about  the  symptoms  and  available  treatments  for  those
suffering  with  mental  health  challenges.

  Gil Hurtado,  Mayor

CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  SPECIAL  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  MAY  28, 2024

CALL  TO ORDER  Gil Hurtado,  Mayor  called  a Special  City  Council  Meeting  to order at 5:33
  p.m.

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Gil Hurtado,  Vice  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Council  Member  Joshua
  Barron,  and Council  Member  Al Rios;  City  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City
  Manager  Rob Houston,  City Attorney  Raul F. Salinas,  Student  Volunteer
  Keon  Sahabi

LATE  Council  Member  Maria  del Pilar  Avalos  arrived  at 5:35 p.m.

CERTIFICATES  The City  Council  presented  Certificates  of Appreciation  to five (5) Girl
  Scouts for their  accomplishments  and volunteer  work.

CERTIFICATES  The City  Council  presented  two (2) Certificates  of Appreciation  to Jose
  Delgado  - Planning  Commissioner  and Jennifer  Cypert  - Parks &
  Recreation  Commissioner.

INTRODUCTION  The City  Council  considered  introducing  the winners  of the Amazon
  Future  Engineer  Scholarships:  Ash Sanchez  1st Place and Wendy  Lopez
  2nd Place, was unanimously  continued  to the City  Council  Meeting  of
  June 11, 2024.

PROCLAMATIONS  The City  Council  issued  a Proclamation  declaring  June as LGBTQ+  Pride
  Month.

PROCLAMATIONS  The City  Counsil  issued  a Proclamation  declaring  June as National  Post-
  Traumatic  Stress Disorder  Awareness  Month.

6
PERSONNEL  RF.CRUITMENT

& SELECTION  The City  Council  unanimously  received  and filed  the list of new and
  promoted  full-time  employees  hired  or promoted  during  April  2024.
   SPECIAL  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF MAY  28, 2024

7
CITY  COUNCIL

APPOINTMENTS  The City  Council  made the following  appointments  to City  Commissions,
  Committees,  and Boards;  the appointments  were ratified  by a majority
  vote of the City  Council.

  Lizette  Ruiz  was appointed  to the Planning  Cornrnission  by Vice Mayor
  Davila.

  Alejanda  Flores  was appointed  to the Parks & Recreation  Commission  and
  removed  from  the Citizens  Advisory  Cornrnittee  by Council  Member
  Avalos.

  Council  Member  Avalos  motioned  to appoint  Ms. Ruiz  to the Planning
  Commission  and Alejanda  Flores  to the Parks & Recreation  Commission
  and seconded  by Vice Mayor  Avalos.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Barron,
  yes; Council  Member  Rios,  yes; Vice Mayor  Davila,  yes; Mayor  Hurtado,
  yes.

CLOSED  SESSION  The Council  Members  recessed  into Closed  Session  at 6:16 p.m. and
  reconvened  at 6:42 p.m. with  all Members  of Council  present.  City
  Attorney  Salinas  reported  the following:

  1.  CONFERENCE  WITH  LEGAL  COtJNSEL  - PENDING
  LITIGATION
  Pursuant  to Government  Code Section  54956.9(a),
  54954.9(b)(3)(C)

  a. Paula Elias  v. City  of South  Gate
  b. Guillermo  Martinez  v. City  of South  Gate, et al.
  c. Nallely  Rincon  v. City  of South  Gate

  On item 1(a), the City  Council  received  a report  regarding  a potential
  resolution  of that matter.  On a motion  made by Vice  Mayor  Davila  and
  seconded  by Council  Member  Barron  and on a vote of 5-0, the City
  Council  authorized  the execution  of settlement  of that matter.

  Item 1(c) was also the subject  of a discussion  by the City Attorney  and a
  recommended  settlement  of that matter.  There  was a motion  made by
  Mayor  Hurtado  and seconded  by Council  Member  Avalos  and on a vote of
  5-0, the City  Council  authorized  the entry  of a settlement  in that matter.

  Both  are subject  to the agreements  being  finalized  and will  be disclosed  in
  accordance  with  the Brown  Act.

  Page 2 of 3
   SPECIAL  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF MAY  28, 2024

  Item 1(b) is a new suit brought  against  the city involving  injury  on one of
  the city's  sidewalks.  On a motion  made by Mayor  Hurtado  and seconded
  by Council  Member  Avalos  and on a vote of 5-0, the City  Council
  authorized  the City Attorney's  Office  to defend  that matter.

ADJOURNMENT  Vice Mayor  Davila  unanimously  adjourned  the meeting  at 6:44 p.m. and
  seconded  by Council  Member  Barron.

PASSED  and APPROVED  this 25'  day of June 2024.
